workstream: D09 — Warm worker + concurrency hardening and Linux-CPU measurement

workerHardening: PaddleServeWorker: stdin 'error' listener kills the worker instead of leaving requests hanging when the pipe breaks (EPIPE) while the process stays alive
PaddleServeWorker.detect: write path guarded — destroyed/unwritable stdin rejects the pending request with PaddleWorkerError instead of throwing synchronously or hanging

New PaddleWorkerSupervisor (bounded restarts, default maxRestarts=2): a crashed worker is respawned on the next detect so subsequent requests are served warm; restart budget exhaustion rejects cleanly

startPaddleWorker now returns the supervisor; analyzeVideo.ts updated to the supervisor type (worker-first with one-shot fallback behavior unchanged, --no-paddle-worker opt-out unchanged, --two-pass still OFF by default)
regressionTestsAdded: concurrent responses matched by id even when the worker replies out of order
stdin closed while process alive -> request rejects with PaddleWorkerError (was: test-observed hang until timeout before the stdin error listener fix)
supervisor restarts a crashed worker and serves subsequent requests (spawns=2, restarts=1)
dispose with in-flight requests rejects them and leaves no process

latencyResults.provenance: wall-clock via Date.now() around real detect_paddle.py / ball_candidates.py invocations; 3 runs per clip per mode (plus 5 extra warm runs on wm-volley-02); one-shot includes python+model startup per call, warm uses a single pre-started worker; warm-worker one-time startup 2663-2700 ms not included in per-request numbers

warmExtendedRuns.note: initial 3-run warm concurrent median lost to sequential by 288 ms with overlapping spread (one 9816 ms outlier), so 5 more alternating runs were collected

afnSaseboRally1.windowMs: paddle 2100-4100 stride 1; ball window per harness

conclusions: Warm worker beats one-shot by ~2.5-3.0 s per prep on this box (python+torch+model startup amortized): e.g. rally1 one-shot seq median 11194 ms vs warm seq median 8680 ms

Concurrent (C08 flag behavior) beats sequential on median in all four mode combinations on both clips; the win is bounded by ball-prep time (0.9-1.5 s) minus CPU contention: os-volley -590 ms, os-rally1 -1389 ms, warm-rally1 -481 ms, warm-volley -248 ms (extended runs)
Because concurrency wins on median in every tested combination, no adaptive scheduler was added; the existing C08 flag behavior is kept as-is

HONEST NEGATIVE: the warm+concurrent win on wm-volley-02 is small (~250 ms) and one initial run inverted (9816 ms concurrent vs 8273 ms sequential) — under heavier CPU contention than this idle 8-thread box the concurrency benefit could vanish; numbers are LINUX-CPU NOT-MAC and say nothing about on-device iOS latency

defectsFoundAndFixed.defect: worker stdin closing (EPIPE) while the process stays alive left the pending request hanging until the request timeout
defectsFoundAndFixed.fix: stdin 'error' listener kills the worker (rejecting all pending requests immediately); write path also rejects when stdin is destroyed/unwritable
defectsFoundAndFixed.regressionTest: packages/swing-lab/test/paddleWorker.test.ts: 'rejects (not crashes) when the worker's stdin closes while it stays alive'

defectsFoundAndFixed.defect: a crashed worker was never restarted — every later paddle window silently paid the one-shot fallback cost for the rest of the run
defectsFoundAndFixed.fix: PaddleWorkerSupervisor with bounded restarts (default 2) wraps the worker; analyzeVideo.ts uses it via startPaddleWorker
defectsFoundAndFixed.regressionTest: supervisor restart + restart-budget tests in paddleWorker.test.ts
